definitions.explanation: Three children born to the same mother at one birth.
A young child of about three. This older sense survives mainly in the proverb below.

examples.japanese: あの{家|いえ}は{三|み}つ{子|ご}の{育児|いくじ}で{大変|たいへん}だ。
examples.english: That household has a hard time raising triplets.

examples.japanese: {双子|ふたご}でも{育児|いくじ}は{大変|たいへん}なのに、{三|み}つ{子|ご}となればなおさらだ。
examples.english: Raising twins is hard enough, so with triplets it is even more so.

examples.japanese: {三|み}つ{子|ご}の{魂|たましい}{百|ひゃく}まで。
examples.english: The soul of a three-year-old lasts until a hundred. (A child's nature stays for life.)

examples.japanese: {三|み}つ{子|ご}のころの{性格|せいかく}は{大人|おとな}になっても{変|か}わらないと{言|い}われる。
examples.english: It is said that one's character at age three does not change even in adulthood.

examples.japanese: 「{三|み}つ{子|ご}の{魂|たましい}{百|ひゃく}まで」ということわざは、{幼|おさな}いころの{性質|せいしつ}が{一生|いっしょう}{続|つづ}くという{意味|いみ}だ。
examples.english: The proverb "the soul of a three-year-old lasts until a hundred" means that one's early nature continues for life.

notes:
Compound of {三|み}つ (three) + {子|こ} (child), with the こ voicing to ご. The everyday meaning is "triplets."

The older sense "three-year-old child" survives chiefly in the proverb {三|み}つ{子|ご}の{魂|たましい}{百|ひゃく}まで (a person's nature in early childhood remains for life).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {三|み}つ{子|ご}を{産|う}む: to give birth to triplets
- {三|み}つ{子|ご}の{兄弟|きょうだい}: triplet siblings

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {双子|ふたご}: twins — two children born together
- {四|よ}つ{子|ご}: quadruplets — the same pattern with four
